summary: __thiscall linked-list node accessor: if the requested index a2 is at least the count this[71] it returns 0; otherwise it walks the list from the head this[72] following the next pointer at node + 0x20 (each element a _DWORD) for a2 steps, breaking early when the next pointer is null, and returns the reached node pointer (index a2 or the last reachable node). Existing analysis names it LinkedListNodeGetByIndex.

operations.description: Out-of-range guard: when a2 >= this[71] (count read at +0x11C) the function returns 0 immediately.
result = this[72] (head pointer read at +0x120) starts the walk.
Walk loop: for i = 0 while i < a2, advance result to the next node via the next pointer at node + 0x20.
Early break: if the next pointer at result + 0x20 is null the walk stops at the current node.
Returns the node pointer at index a2, or the last reachable node when the chain ends early.
Called by GlobalGuardedFieldReader (0x004F91B0), GuardedFieldAccessor (0x004F9200) and sub_53F3F0 (0x0053F3F0).

unresolved: The packet identifies the node next pointer with base *(this+0x140) (offset 0x20); the relationship between that base and the returned node pointer is not established.
Whether this[71] is an exact count or a max index bound is inferred from the guard only.
Returning the last reachable node (rather than null) when the chain is shorter than a2 is evident from the code but its semantic intent is unknown.
